# Problem 1

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
```

```{r problem1}
homicide_df =
  read_csv(
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/washingtonpost/data-homicides/master/homicide-data.csv",
    na = c("", "Unknown"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) |>
  mutate(
    city_state = str_c(city, state, sep = ", "),
    resolved = if_else(disposition == "Closed by arrest", 1, 0),
    victim_age = as.numeric(victim_age)
  ) |>
  filter(
    !city_state %in% c(
      "Dallas, TX",
      "Phoenix, AZ",
      "Kansas City, MO",
      "Tulsa, AL"
    ),
    victim_race %in% c("White", "Black")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    victim_sex = factor(victim_sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    victim_race = factor(victim_race, levels = c("White", "Black"))
  )

homicide_df

baltimore_df =
  homicide_df |>
  filter(city_state == "Baltimore, MD")

baltimore_fit =
  glm(
    resolved ~ victim_age + victim_sex + victim_race,
    data = baltimore_df,
    family = binomial()
  )

baltimore_fit

baltimore_results =
  baltimore_fit |>
  broom::tidy(
    conf.int = TRUE,
    exponentiate = TRUE
  ) |>
  filter(term == "victim_sexMale") |>
  select(term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high)

baltimore_results |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)

city_results =
  homicide_df |>
  group_by(city_state) |>
  nest() |>
  mutate(
    model = map(
      data,
      ~ glm(
        resolved ~ victim_age + victim_sex + victim_race,
        data = .x,
        family = binomial()
      )
    ),
    results = map(
      model,
      ~ broom::tidy(
        .x,
        conf.int = TRUE,
        exponentiate = TRUE
      )
    )
  ) |>
  select(city_state, results) |>
  unnest(results) |>
  filter(term == "victim_sexMale") |>
  select(city_state, estimate, conf.low, conf.high) |>
  ungroup()

city_results |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

```{r problem1_plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=12}
city_results |>
  mutate(
    city_state = fct_reorder(city_state, estimate)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = city_state, y = estimate)) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
    width = 0.2,
    color = "steelblue"
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "red"
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Adjusted Odds Ratios for Homicide Resolution by City",
    subtitle = "Male victims compared with female victims",
    x = "City",
    y = "Adjusted Odds Ratio (95% CI)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
Most cities had odds ratios below 1, meaning that homicides involving male victims generally had lower odds of being solved than those involving female victims after adjusting for age and race. However, several cities had confidence intervals that included 1, so the difference was not statistically significant in those cities. Some cities also had wider confidence intervals, suggesting that their estimates were less precise.

# Problem 2

```{r problem2_data, message=FALSE}
library(p8105.datasets)
data("weather_df")

weather_df =
  weather_df |>
  select(tmax, tmin, prcp) |>
  drop_na()

weather_df
```

```{r problem2_bootstrap_function}
boot_sample = function(df) {
  sample_frac(df, size = 1, replace = TRUE)
}
```

```{r problem2_bootstrap_simulation}
set.seed(123)

boot_results =
  tibble(
    replicate = 1:5000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    boot_sample = map(
      replicate, ~ boot_sample(weather_df)
    ),
    model = map(
      boot_sample,
      ~ lm(tmax ~ tmin + prcp, data = .x)
    ),
    glance_results = map(model, broom::glance),
    tidy_results = map(model, broom::tidy)
  )

boot_results
```

```{r problem2_r_squared}
r_squared_results =
  boot_results |>
  select(replicate, glance_results) |>
  unnest(glance_results) |>
  select(replicate, r.squared)

r_squared_results
```

```{r problem2_beta_ratio}
beta_results =
  boot_results |>
  select(replicate, tidy_results) |>
  unnest(tidy_results) |>
  filter(term %in% c("tmin", "prcp")) |>
  select(replicate, term, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = term,
    values_from = estimate
  ) |>
  mutate(
    beta_ratio = tmin / prcp
  ) |>
  select(replicate, beta_ratio)

beta_results
```

```{r problem2_combine}
bootstrap_estimates =
  left_join(
    r_squared_results,
    beta_results,
    by = "replicate"
  )

bootstrap_estimates
```

```{r problem2_r_squared_plot}
bootstrap_estimates |>
  ggplot(aes(x = r.squared)) +
  geom_density(
    fill = "steelblue",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Bootstrap Distribution of R-squared",
    x = "R-squared",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
The bootstrap distribution of R-squared is roughly bell-shaped with a slight left skew and is centered around 0.941. The estimates are concentrated within a narrow range, suggesting that R-squared remains mostly consistent across bootstrap samples. The 95% bootstrap confidence interval is (0.9344, 0.9466).

```{r problem2_beta_ratio_plot}
bootstrap_estimates |>
  ggplot(aes(x = beta_ratio)) +
  geom_density(
    fill = "steelblue",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Bootstrap Distribution of the Coefficient Ratio",
    x = expression(hat(beta)[1] / hat(beta)[2]),
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The bootstrap distribution of the coefficient ratio is left-skewed, with a longer tail toward more negative values. The mean estimate is −185.4894, and the 95% bootstrap confidence interval is (−277.1703, −125.7063).

```{r problem2_confidence_intervals}
bootstrap_ci =
  bootstrap_estimates |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(r.squared, beta_ratio),
    names_to = "statistic",
    values_to = "estimate"
  ) |>
  group_by(statistic) |>
  summarize(
    mean_estimate = mean(estimate),
    conf.low = quantile(estimate, 0.025),
    conf.high = quantile(estimate, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bootstrap_ci |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

# Problem 3

```{r problem3_data, message=FALSE}
library(modelr)
library(janitor)

birthweight_df =
  read_csv("data/birthweight.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    babysex = factor(
      babysex,
      levels = c(1, 2),
      labels = c("Male", "Female")
    ),
    frace = factor(
      frace,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9),
      labels = c("White", "Black", "Asian",
                 "Puerto Rican", "Other", "Unknown")
    ),
    mrace = factor(
      mrace,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 8),
      labels = c("White", "Black", "Asian",
                 "Puerto Rican", "Other")
    ),
    malform = factor(
      malform,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("Absent", "Present")
    )
  )

birthweight_df
```

```{r problem3_missing_values}
birthweight_df |>
  summarize(
    across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "missing"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r problem3_proposed_model}
my_model =
  lm(
    bwt ~ bhead + blength + gaweeks + babysex +
      smoken + ppbmi + wtgain + momage,
    data = birthweight_df
  )

my_model |>
  broom::tidy() |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

```{r problem3_model_summary}
my_model |>
  broom::glance() |>
  select(r.squared, adj.r.squared, sigma) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

I selected variables based on their potential relationship with birthweight. Head circumference, birth length, gestational age, and baby sex were included to account for differences in fetal growth. I also included maternal smoking, pre-pregnancy BMI, weight gain during pregnancy, and maternal age because these factors may be related to birthweight. I avoided including maternal weight variables that were closely related to each other to reduce multicollinearity. The model explained approximately 69.9% of the variation in birthweight.

```{r problem3_residual_plot}
birthweight_df |>
  add_predictions(my_model) |>
  add_residuals(my_model) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pred, y = resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    color = "red",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Residuals vs Fitted Values",
    x = "Fitted Birthweight (grams)",
    y = "Residuals (grams)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r problem3_comparison_model1}
model_1 =
  lm(
    bwt ~ blength + gaweeks,
    data = birthweight_df
  )
```

```{r problem3_comparison_model2}
model_2 =
  lm(
    bwt ~ bhead * blength * babysex,
    data = birthweight_df
  )
```

```{r problem3_cross_validation}
set.seed(123)

cv_df =
  crossv_mc(
    birthweight_df,
    n = 100,
    test = 0.2
  ) |>
  mutate(
    train = map(train, as_tibble),
    test = map(test, as_tibble)
  )

cv_df
```

```{r problem3_cv_models}
cv_results =
  cv_df |>
  mutate(
    my_model = map(
      train,
      ~ lm(
        bwt ~ bhead + blength + gaweeks + babysex +
          smoken + ppbmi + wtgain + momage,
        data = .x
      )
    ),
    model_1 = map(
      train,
      ~ lm(bwt ~ blength + gaweeks, data = .x)
    ),
    model_2 = map(
      train,
      ~ lm(bwt ~ bhead * blength * babysex, data = .x)
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    rmse_my_model = map2_dbl(my_model, test, rmse),
    rmse_model_1 = map2_dbl(model_1, test, rmse),
    rmse_model_2 = map2_dbl(model_2, test, rmse)
  )

cv_results
```

```{r problem3_cv_wrangle}
cv_plot_df =
  cv_results |>
  select(starts_with("rmse_")) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "model",
    values_to = "rmse"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    model = recode(
      model,
      rmse_my_model = "Proposed Model",
      rmse_model_1 = "Length + Gestational Age",
      rmse_model_2 = "Head, Length, Sex + Interactions"
    )
  )

cv_plot_df
```

```{r problem3_cv_plot}
cv_plot_df |>
  mutate(
    model = fct_reorder(model, rmse)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = model, y = rmse)) +
  geom_violin(
    fill = "steelblue",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.1,
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Cross-Validated Prediction Error",
    x = "Regression Model",
    y = "RMSE (grams)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The proposed model had the lowest mean RMSE of 281.68 grams, followed by the interaction model at 288.38 grams. The model using only birth length and gestational age had the highest mean RMSE of 330.71 grams. The results suggest that including additional fetal and maternal characteristics improves birthweight prediction.

```{r problem3_cv_summary}
cv_plot_df |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarize(
    mean_rmse = mean(rmse),
    median_rmse = median(rmse),
    sd_rmse = sd(rmse),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(mean_rmse) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```
